adjudicator: Claude Opus 5, working blind from premise/hypothesis pairs alone
method: For each pair I first asked whether a world could satisfy every word of the premise while the hypothesis was false (test 1), then whether a world could satisfy the premise with the hypothesis true (test 2), treating reported speech, hedges, quantifiers like 'most'/'mostly', and mere temporal sequence as leaving things open rather than settling them. Only if both held did I ask whether an ordinary hearer would feel pulled toward the hypothesis (test 3). I read names and pronouns as coreferring with the obvious speaker where the premise gave no competing referent, but I refused to import world-knowledge causation, social roles, or motives that the words never state.

cases.rationale: The premise reports what Marcus said, not what he will do, and 'after work' need not fall in the evening. Both stay open, and the inference is the natural one.
'Her brother Toby' asserts the relation as part of naming him; the hypothesis cannot be false while the premise stands.
Untouched dinner and time upstairs are consistent with illness, absorption or sleep; the premise names no feeling. The upset reading is the one a hearer reaches for.
'Never in his life cooked a meal for another person' excludes cooking for his mother on Sundays.
The premise asserts only that Gran swears it; a sworn family claim can be wrong. It is exactly the inference the sentence invites.
Two facts placed side by side — a change and an improvement — do not assert that one produced the other, but the juxtaposition strongly invites it.
Being the one who always fixes them is not the same as holding responsibility for them; he could be the only competent volunteer. The inference is tempting all the same.
'Got back from Lisbon last night' cannot be true unless the speaker was in Lisbon beforehand.
Sitting at the back taking notes is as consistent with a reporter, an observer or management as with a member; attendance is not membership. Readers will assume membership anyway.
No age and no comparison class appear anywhere in the premise, so nothing settles a comparison with other children; the admiring report still tempts a hearer toward precocity.
Browsing flats is compatible with idle curiosity, research for someone else, or a fantasy; intention is never stated. The inference is the obvious one.
'I was furious with Cal all evening' states the hypothesis in other words.

The premise reports a chance meeting and her appearance and says nothing whatever about how the relationship ended; 'bad terms' is one of many equally unsupported possibilities, and nothing in the words pulls toward it.
The premise denies any involvement of the wiring and names a different origin.
The identifying clause 'the one who wrote the letter to the council' attaches that act to Delia as part of picking her out.
'Most mornings' explicitly falls short of every day, and being at the pool is not necessarily swimming; yet daily swimming is compatible with the premise and is what a hearer takes away.
The premise denies outright that Ines is the manager and assigns the role to someone else.
Unable to complete one length then, four hundred metres now, is improvement between those two points by the plain meaning of the words.
Turning up to working parties with her own fork is fully consistent with a helper, neighbour or waiting-list volunteer holding no plot. The inference is natural.
A fountain switched back on dates the move to warm weather at best, and spring fits 'finally' at least as well as summer; the season is never named. A reader still leans to summer.
Handing in one's notice is by definition the act of leaving, and the premise states it as a settled plan with the letter already printed.
Going quiet afterwards has many causes — tiredness, an unrelated thought — and the premise names none. The troubled reading is the tempting one.
The premise records a change and a later improvement without claiming a link; the causal reading is nonetheless what the sentence invites.
Persistent texting is equally consistent with a relative, colleague or acquaintance, and the mild irritation cuts slightly against friendship. Readers will still assume it.
'I don't think that's actually his name' is a hedged belief, not an assertion that it isn't; the speaker could be wrong. The hedge still points the hearer that way.
'Every single winter, without fail' asserts repeated occurrence, which is more than once.
Bookkeeping and ordering are ordinary employee or contractor duties and say nothing about ownership; the breadth of the role nonetheless tempts a reader toward a stake in the business.
Having joined in March and attended every rehearsal since asserts current membership.
'Not a stroke of it different' excludes a great deal of change.
Never once late in three years excludes a late arrival last winter; I read the third-person hypothesis as referring to the same speaker, which is the only sensible reading available.

Asking twice about a ring is at least as consistent with wanting it herself or hinting as with proposing to anyone; the premise names no intention. The proposal reading is still a recognisable temptation.
'Wasn't nervous at all' before the recital excludes anxiety in the run-up to it.
The premise states the causal relation outright with 'because'; the hypothesis restates it.
'Never actually met' over six years excludes meeting at a conference last year.
The premise places the same man at the neighbours' house but says nothing about what he did there; he might have been fitting a shower or visiting. The boiler reading is strongly invited.
Sharing a stop occasionally is consistent with different routes or opposite directions; no bus is identified. Readers assume the same bus anyway.
Distributing the agenda at the front is as much a secretary's or helper's task as a chair's; the premise assigns no authority. The inference is the tempting one.
'Neither of the Haldane boys belongs' covers the elder boy explicitly.
Walking to the shop unaided shows progress, not completed recovery, which the premise never claims. A hearer will nonetheless take it as recovery.
Silence since Tuesday is exactly the absence of information about her whereabouts; she may have been discharged. The natural reading is that she is still in.
The speaker denies any plan to sell and reports refusing askers; taking the third-person hypothesis to be about that same speaker, it is excluded.
The premise reports only what Yusuf keeps saying, which leaves his actual state open in either direction; the repetition tempts a hearer toward protesting too much.
'Since' marks time, not cause, and the increase could have other sources; the causal reading is the one the sentence invites.

Not knowing their names after eleven years is as consistent with the speaker's own reserve as with the neighbours' coldness, and no behaviour of theirs is described. A reader is still tempted to blame them.
'Wasn't Rosa at all' denies that the name was hers.
Twice in one month is compatible with a one-off residency or a first booking; regularity is a pattern over time the premise does not establish. 'Already' pulls a hearer toward it.
Shadowing for a week could be induction, cover, or familiarisation without any handover; the premise states no plan. Taking over is the obvious guess.
That half the club drinks there and Priya is always there does not put Priya in the club; the pub has other customers. The overlap is very tempting all the same.
One stopped behaviour is not a developmental trend and could reflect a rule, a mood or fear rather than maturing. The inference is the natural family reading.
The past tense describes a past habit without asserting it has ended; he may still do it. The tense nonetheless strongly implies discontinuation.
Buying shoes shows current investment, not future intention, and 'again' hints at past lapses; intention is never stated. The inference is the one being invited.
Crying at a ceremony is compatible with relief, grief, overwhelm or embarrassment; the premise names no emotion. Happiness is what a reader assumes.
The premise gives a sequence of two events, not a cause, and does not even say the household moved. The causal reading is strongly invited.
A guest may be a sister, a friend or a colleague, and the lack of introductions is if anything odd for a partner; nothing states a relationship. Readers read her as a date.
'Looks like' is a resemblance judgement about a photo, which is exactly the sort of thing that turns out wrong. The identification is the tempting inference.
'Mostly' explicitly admits exceptions, and this past Sunday could be one; the premise never mentions it. A hearer will still expect the call happened.
'As chair of the residents' committee' asserts the speaker's office as the ground of the claim.
A photo hung among team pictures could honour a coach, a groundsman, a benefactor or someone who died; playing is never stated. The inference is the obvious one.
Ceasing to ask shows changed behaviour, which could be confidence without skill or reluctance to ask; competence is not asserted. The intended reading is very tempting.
Committing to a year of lessons shows seriousness about the language, not a destination, and Portuguese is spoken well beyond Portugal; no trip is mentioned. The inference still tempts.
